title: Invert Binary Tree
oneLinerQuestion: Invert a binary tree so that left and right children are swapped recursively across all levels.
explanation:
Problem Intuition: The Invert Binary Tree problem asks us to invert or mirror a binary tree such that for every node, its left and right subtrees are swapped across its vertical axis. Because a tree is inherently recursive, solving the problem for the entire tree decomposes into solving the identical subproblem for every descendant subtree: each node must swap its direct left and right child pointers, while the descendant trees attached to those children are themselves recursively inverted. Whether approached top-down (pre-order) or bottom-up (post-order), visiting every node and exchanging its pointer references achieves a complete reflection in-place in linear time.

- Step 1: Base Case & Recursion Guard — If `root === null`, the tree or subtree is empty; we immediately return `null`. This terminates recursive calls on leaf node descendants.

- Step 2: Pointer Swap Execution — For the current active node `root`, we swap its direct left and right pointers: `const temp = root.left; root.left = root.right; root.right = temp`. (Alternatively, this swap can occur post-order after recursive calls resolve).

- Step 3: Recursive Left Subtree Inversion — We recursively invoke the inversion routine on the newly assigned left branch: `invertTree(root.left)`. In the context of a right subtree containing [6, 9], once swapped over, its own children recursively invert internally.

- Step 4: Recursive Right Subtree Inversion — We recursively invoke the inversion routine on the newly assigned right branch: `invertTree(root.right)` to mirror all remaining descendant nodes.

- Step 5: Termination & Root Propagation — After the subtrees of the current node have completed their mutual pointer exchanges, we return `root`.

- Complexity & Memory Guarantees — Time Complexity: O(N) where N is the total number of nodes in the binary tree, as every node is visited exactly once. Space Complexity: O(H) auxiliary space on the call stack, where H is the height of the tree (O(log N) for a balanced tree and O(N) in the worst case for a skewed degenerate tree).
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION invertTree(root):
    IF root IS NULL THEN RETURN NULL
    temp = root.left
    root.left = invertTree(root.right)
    root.right = invertTree(temp)
    RETURN root
END FUNCTION

Line 4: Recurse into right subtree Node(7). Inspect its children: left=6, right=9.
Lines 4-5: Swap 7's children: temp = 6; 7.left = 9; 7.right = 6. Children animate across 7's axis.
Line 4: Back at root Node(4). Prepare to swap left subtree (Node 2) and right subtree (Node 7 and its children).
Lines 4-5: Swap root's children: root.left = 7 (along with leaves 9 and 6), root.right = 2. Subtrees animate across main mirror axis.
Line 7: Inversion complete! Left child is now 7 (with children 9, 6) and right child is now 2. RETURN root.
